- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- In low-sentiment periods with mean-reverting price behavior, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch momentum.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 3 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to average out; use 14-day EWMA of price + sentiment to smooth forecast.
